subject: English
title: Creative Writing Unit — Y7 English
tool_context: Creative writing unit — students read literary texts as writers, noticing how authors use language features and literary devices, then experiment with those devices in their own creative text. The unit activates Literature examining and creating strands alongside Literacy creating strands. Language concept standards (identity, sentence structure) are activated as craft tools for voice and effect.
progression_endpoint: Students produce a crafted literary text that demonstrates deliberate experimentation with at least two language features or literary devices encountered in reading, with editing decisions that show awareness of how specific choices create meaning and effect for a reader.

phases.label: Reading as a Writer
phases.checkpoint: Students can identify specific language features and literary devices in source texts and explain what effect each creates — they are reading as writers, not just as readers, and have a repertoire of craft moves to attempt.

waypoints.note: Establishing the context of source texts — who wrote this, when, and why — before reading as a writer begins.
Reading to notice how narrative elements work — not to analyse meaning but to see craft decisions a writer makes.
Building a repertoire of literary device names and effects — the vocabulary students need to name what they want to try.
Noticing how language expresses identity in source texts — introduced here as a reading observation before students consider their own writer's voice.
Noticing layers of meaning — reading a device for what it does at the literal level and what it suggests beyond that.

phases.label: Experimenting
phases.checkpoint: Students can attempt at least two craft moves from their reading — experimenting with a literary device or language feature in short writing tasks — and can identify what they were trying and whether it worked.

waypoints.note: Identifying specific devices from source texts to try — the connection between reading and attempted craft.
Experimenting with language as identity construction — developing a writer's voice by making deliberate language choices that create a character or narrator identity.
Experimenting with how narrative elements combine — trying different character/setting/event combinations in short drafts before committing to a full piece.
Experimenting with sentence structure for effect — trying complex and compound-complex sentences to elaborate or extend ideas in creative writing.
Sentence structure as deliberate choice — experimenting with variation (simple for impact, complex for development) in short creative pieces.

phases.label: Drafting
phases.checkpoint: Students can produce a complete draft creative text that incorporates at least two deliberate craft choices from their experimentation phase, with a developed narrative or lyric shape and a recognisable writer's voice.

waypoints.note: Planning the creative text — purpose (imaginative), audience, and structural shape before drafting the full piece.
Creating the full draft — the integration point where experimentation becomes a sustained piece.
Creating and editing the draft — making deliberate structural and language choices and beginning to revise for effect.

phases.label: Publishing
phases.checkpoint: Students can publish a crafted literary text with evidence of deliberate editing decisions, and present or share it in a way that demonstrates awareness of audience — the text shows the integrated craft knowledge developed across the unit.

waypoints.note: Final editing — removing unnecessary repetition, varying sentence structures for effect, reviewing craft choices.
Planning how to present or share the creative work — audience and mode choices for publication or performance.
Delivering or publishing — using voice features or presentation choices that serve the creative text's effect.
